packs.title: Icons and Neighborhoods
packs.promise: Discover Dallas through its skyline, museums, gardens and neighborhood streets.

q.s: Give one documented detail time to settle.
st: Visit an open museum exhibit at your own pace.
Choose one museum-presented fact about Kennedy’s life, legacy or the historical context, recording its source.
After leaving the exhibit, pause for a minute and write why that detail stayed with you.

q.s: Respond to one color without reproducing an entire work.
st: Choose a work in an open collection gallery.
Read the label and note the credited artist or maker as presented.
Make a tiny original color study inspired by one relationship in the work, and add its source credit in your note.

q.s: Find rhythm in a neighborhood’s public-facing art.
st: Choose an open daylight sidewalk view of a mural.
Find one repeated form and one interruption in the repetition.
Record the contrast and the artist credit if displayed, without entering private property.

packs.title: Forms between Performances
packs.promise: Read a neighborhood of art through the spaces around it.

q.s: Collect three clues to a place made for staying.
st: Choose an open path outside event equipment and play areas.
Find a planted edge, a place to rest and a clear through-route. Compare how each occupies its own patch of ground.
Make a three-part park toolkit and choose the feature that makes the whole space easiest to use.

q.s: Find three different ways a building meets the street.
st: Observe the frontage from the public sidewalk without entering the ticketed museum or garden.
Find a solid surface, a transparent surface and an open gap or recess.
Describe which boundary feels most open and why.

q.t: Where a Curve Meets a Corner
q.s: Collect a building’s changes of direction.
st: Choose a public-sidewalk view clear of arrivals and doors.
Find a curve, a straight edge and a place where the two seem to meet.
Draw three direction marks and name the one that gives the facade its strongest movement.
